1.note: Here, **all the earth** represents all the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all you people who live on the earth]

2.note: Here, **name** represents who Yahweh is. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [bless everything that he is]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that he is the one who saves]

The psalmist is using **from day to day** as a common expression of his culture to mean “continually” or “regularly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [every day]

3.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that he is extremely great]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [recount his marvelous deeds]

4.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Because]

The expression **is to be praised** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and everyone should praise him]

The expression **He is to be feared** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Everyone should fear him]

5.note: Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [You see,]

6.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **Splendor** and **majesty**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [His presence is splendid and majestic]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **Strength** and **beauty**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [He is strong and beautiful]
Here, **to his face** represents “in his presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [are in his presence]

7.note: These two phrases **Ascribe to Yahweh** and **ascribe to Yahweh** repeat the same meaning. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating it again. If it would be helpful to your readers, you say this once and express the emphasis in another way, as in the UST.

The psalmist is using this possessive form to mean clans that belong to various peoples or clans from among the peoples. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [all clans in all peoples]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **glory** and **strength**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [the fact that he is glorious and strong]

8.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Praise Yahweh because he is the glorious one]
Here, **name** represents who God is. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the glory of who he is]

9.note: To **Bow down** was a symbolic action by which people showed reverence and submission to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [Bow down in worship]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **splendor** and **holiness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [because he is splendid and holy]

To **tremble** was a symbolic action by which people showed reverent fear and awe before God’s holy presence. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [tremble in reverent awe]

The psalmist is using **from his face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of” or “on account of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of him]

Here, **all the earth** represents all the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all you people of the earth]

10.note: The expression **the world is established** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [he established the world]

The expression **it cannot be shaken** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [nothing can shake it]

This could mean: (1) Yahweh always judges the peoples with evenness, as in the UST, or (2) on the future day of judgment, Yahweh will judge the peoples with evenness. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will judge]

11.q: יִשְׂמְח֣וּ הַ֭⁠שָּׁמַיִם וְ⁠תָגֵ֣ל הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ יִֽרְעַ֥ם הַ֝⁠יָּ֗ם
11.note: Here the psalmist is calling on the heavens, earth, and sea to respond with praise to Yahweh. This is the author’s way of expressing that all of creation should respond to Yahweh with joy and praise. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team on how you could express this with statements about what creation should do, as modeled in the UST.

By **its fullness**, the psalmist means all of the creatures that fill the sea. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and all of the creatures that fill it]

This could mean: (1) **the heavens** and **the earth** represent those who dwell in those places. Alternate translation: [Let those who live in the heavens be glad and let those who live on the earth rejoice] or (2) the heavens and the earth are spoken of as if they had emotions like people have. Alternate translation: [The heavens should be glad and the earth should rejoice]

12.q: יַעֲלֹ֣ז שָׂ֭דַי וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁר־בּ֑⁠וֹ אָ֥ז יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ כָּל־עֲצֵי־יָֽעַר
12.note: Here the psalmist is speaking of **fields** and **trees** as if they were living things that could **rejoice** and **shout for joy**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Let it be as though the fields and all that is in them are celebrating. Then let it be as though all the trees in the forest are shouting happily]

13.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before]

These two phrases **for he is coming** and **for he is coming** are the same. The words are repeated to emphasize their meaning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [for it is sure that he is coming]

Here, **the earth** represents the people who live on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of the earth]

Here, **the world** represents everyone who lives in the world. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everyone in the world]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [righteously]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [faithfully]

The terms **the earth** and **the world** mean similar things. The psalmist is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [everyone … everyone]

The writer is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and he will judge the peoples with his faithfulness]
